question: A bookmaker offers odds of 1.90 on both sides of an even match. Someone bets £100 on each side. Pounds lost?
move: Add up every price on offer to see what the seller keeps.
ask: When I am offered a choice of deals, have I checked what the seller keeps whichever I pick?
trap: Taking odds of 1.90 on each side as a fair price.
hint: Compare the total staked with what the winning bet pays back.
reference: Raymond D. Sauer, The Economics of Wagering Markets, Journal of Economic Literature, 1998
